summary: Manner and agent-oriented adverbs in MTT-semantics via dependent event types: a 21-line near-verbatim transcription of Appendix A7.8 of Chatzikyriakidis & Luo (2020), realizing EvtM(m) and EvtAM(a,m) as singleton inductives Evt_m/Evt_ma, defining the manner adverb illegibly_m as P x E /\ illegible_m m and the agent-oriented illegibly_a analogously, and proving the book's own theorem MANNER (example 6.2: John wrote illegibly => John wrote in an illegible manner). Loads Coq_book_ontology (CN:=Set, coercion hierarchy, John:Man). The file silently repairs the book's ill-typed printed appendix code by typing illegible of manners rather than events.

sources.citation: Chatzikyriakidis, S. & Luo, Z. (2020). Formal Semantics in Modern Type Theories. Wiley/ISTE. §4.5.2 (manner, agent-oriented and speech-act adverbs, eqs. 4.56-4.65), §6.3.1 (example 6.2), Appendix A7.8 (Manner adverbs).
Luo, Z. & Soloviev, S. (2017). Dependent event types (cited by the book as the origin of EvtA/EvtM/EvtAM; discussed in book §7.2).

definitions_mapped.coq: Inductive Evt_m : Manner -> Type / Evt_ma : Manner -> Agent -> Type (single constructor)
definitions_mapped.source: EvtM(m), EvtAM(a,m) dependent event types (book §4.5.2, (4.57)-(4.62); Luo & Soloviev 2017)
definitions_mapped.note: singleton inductives — every Evt_m m has exactly one inhabitant, so all events of a given manner are identified; this is the book's own Appendix A7.8 code, but the theory's event types are not singletons; no theorem exploits the degeneracy

definitions_mapped.coq: illegible_m : Manner -> Prop; illegible_ma : Manner -> Agent -> Prop
definitions_mapped.source: illegible : EvtM(m) -> Prop in display (4.58)/(4.61) and §6.3.1 code; appendix A7.8 prints the ill-typed 'forall m: Manner, EVT_m m -> Prop'
definitions_mapped.note: the file predicates illegibility of the manner (and manner+agent pair), not the event — this repairs the appendix misprint and matches the prose (p. 92: the manner, not the event, is illegible) but diverges from the book's official displayed definition

definitions_mapped.coq: illegibly_m := fun m A P x E => P x E /\ illegible_m m
definitions_mapped.source: ADV_manner (4.58)/(4.61): illegibly(P,x,E) = P(x,E) /\ illegible(E); Appendix A7.8 illegibly_m
definitions_mapped.note: exact to Appendix A7.8 (modulo its repaired Parameter type); the conjunct predicates the manner where (4.58) predicates the event — the source is internally inconsistent between its display, its §6.3.1 inline code, and its appendix

definitions_mapped.coq: illegibly_a := fun m a A P x E => P x E /\ illegible_ma m a
definitions_mapped.note: defined but no theorem uses it — also true in the book's appendix

definitions_mapped.coq: write : forall m, Human -> Evt_m m -> Prop; Agent : CN; witnesses m : Manner, u : Evt_m m; John via Load Coq_book_ontology
definitions_mapped.source: A7.8 verbatim; ontology from the book's Coq appendices
definitions_mapped.note: the Human <= Agent subtyping and the coercions among dependent event types (EvtAM <= EvtA <= Event, book §7.2) are absent; Agent serves only as an index

definitions_mapped.source: speech-act adverbs frankly/EvtUM(u,m), (4.63)-(4.65); the veridical projection 'he wrote illegibly => he wrote' asserted after (4.58); dependent-event-type subtyping of §7.2
definitions_mapped.note: the veridical projection is one conjunct-elimination away from illegibly_m but is never stated

theorems.name: MANNER
theorems.source_claim: Book Appendix A7.8 theorem MANNER = example (6.2): John wrote illegibly => John wrote in an illegible manner
theorems.note: the book's own statement, reproduced exactly — but it is an existentially quantified implication witnessed by declared constants m, u, true by conjunct projection (cbv; firstorder); essentially trivial per rubric §3 and would be excluded from verified counts; the stronger rendering of (6.2) would be universally quantified over m and e

evidence: The file is a near-verbatim transcription of the book's own Appendix A7.8 Coq code, including its theorem MANNER, which is proved with Qed (grep: 1 theorem, 0 Admitted).

The appendix as printed does not typecheck (constructor EVT_m used as a type; body illegible_m m ill-typed under the printed Parameter); the file's repair — illegible_m : Manner -> Prop — is a changed core definition relative to the book's displayed (4.58)/(4.61) and §6.3.1 code, where illegible : EvtM(m) -> Prop is predicated of the event.

All 7 Parameters are signature-level (types, predicate symbols, witness constants) with no propositional content; the loaded Coq_book_ontology contributes only coercion-function Axioms, likewise non-propositional.
The proved theorem is the book's headline inference (6.2), but in the book's own logically weak existential form, and the companion veridical projection claim after (4.58) is never stated.
simplifications: EvtM(m)/EvtAM(a,m) realized as singleton inductives (one constructor, one inhabitant per index) — the book's own appendix move, but the theory's event types are not singletons
one worked example (illegibly + write) stands in for the whole adverb typology of §4.5.2
omissions: the veridical projection 'he wrote illegibly => he wrote' asserted 'needless to say' after (4.58)
any theorem for the agent-oriented adverb illegibly_a (defined, never used — as in the book)
subtyping among dependent event types and Human <= Agent (book §7.2, Luo & Soloviev 2017)
additions: the type repair of the appendix's ill-typed Parameters (a correction forced by the misprint, not new machinery)

determination_rationale: The only mechanization pressure visible is (a) repairing the source's ill-typed printed appendix code — the book's three renderings of 'illegible' (display 4.58/4.61: of the event; §6.3.1 inline code: of the event; Appendix A7.8: of the manner, ill-typed as printed) are mutually inconsistent, and the file documents a choice among them that preserves the predicted inference (6.2), which is proved — and (b) the singleton-inductive realization of EvtM(m), a simplification the source's own appendix makes. Neither changes the theory's predictions, and the event-predicating variant per (4.58) typechecks without obstruction, so nothing suggests the theory resists as-is mechanization; but the evidence base is one essentially trivial theorem, so this determination is provisional pending a real atlas formalization of dependent event types (Luo & Soloviev 2017) with subtyping.

artifact_classes.description: the MTT's native coercive subtyping among dependent event types (EvtAM(a,m) <= EvtM(m) <= Event; Human <= Agent, book §7.2) is absent; EvtM(m) is realized as a singleton inductive rather than an abstract indexed family, identifying all events of a given manner

source_gap.detail: Book Appendix A7.8 as printed does not typecheck: illegible_m is declared 'forall m: Manner, EVT_m m -> Prop' with the constructor EVT_m used as a type, and even repaired to 'Evt_m m -> Prop' the definition body 'illegible_m m' is ill-typed. Moreover the book's displayed definition (4.58)/(4.61) and its §6.3.1 inline Coq predicate illegible of the event E, while the appendix (and this file) predicate it of the manner m — and the book's own motivating prose (p. 92: 'it is the manner of the event rather than the event itself that is illegible') supports the manner version, so the official display contradicts the prose that introduces it.

notes: Record produced by the 2026-09-05 batch audit sweep; the file predates the atlas zero-axiom discipline (7 signature Parameters here plus legacy 'Load Coq_book_ontology' with its coercion Axioms, none propositional) and its single theorem is trivial under the rubric §3 filter.
